title: Validation contract v1
description: What a release was validated AGAINST. A green validation run is meaningless without this: an estate depends on services it does not own, and 'it came up' says nothing until the reader knows whether the database was the real managed instance or an empty in-cluster stand-in. THE RULE IS REAL BY DEFAULT. A double is permitted only where real is impossible or harmful, and it must carry the justification. An unjustifiable double is a contract violation, not a shortcut. This artifact is also what tells a SUBSCRIBER what their release was validated against, so it is a customer-facing product surface, not test scaffolding.

id.description: Stable identifier, referenced by hash from the channel entry and by id from receipts.

rule.description: Restated in every contract so it cannot be forgotten between one and the next.
rule.const: real by default; each double carries a justification; an unjustifiable double is a contract violation

fidelity.description: real = the actual production-class service; an optional parenthetical qualifier may narrow it (e.g. `real(Stripe test mode)`) but it is still the real implementation. double(<what>) = a substitute that implements the real contract. dummy-endpoint = something that answers but does not implement. absent = not present at all; every claim depending on it is unproven. Anything other than `real` REQUIRES a justification saying why real was impossible or harmful.

justification.description: REQUIRED for any fidelity that is not `real`. Must say why real was impossible or harmful — not why the double was convenient.

proves.description: One line: what this fidelity genuinely establishes.

does_not_prove.description: One line: what a reader must NOT conclude. This field is the point of the document.

endpoint_shape.description: How the estate reaches it during validation, without credentials.

unproven_claims.description: Claims that any `absent` or `dummy-endpoint` dependency makes unavailable. Written out so a receipt cannot accidentally assert them.
